title: Numbers One to Five
label: ch:numbers-one-to-five
canDo: I can say the Sanskrit numerals एक to पञ्च with their dual and gendered forms, and follow पञ्च outward into Punjab, pentagon, and the disputed history of punch.

payoff.summary: Trace pañca out of Sanskrit: into Persian panj-āb, the five waters behind Punjab; into Greek pente in pentagon and pentathlon; and into punch, with the five-ingredients account labelled as common rather than settled. Then count one to five with the dual and the neuter forms the daughter languages inherit, say the cousins and the sound laws between them, and pick out ञ.
payoff.note: The payoff moves from SA-C06-pancha-travels (sequence 330) to its continuation SA-C06-pancha-travels-more (333), the chapter's last chapter-6 lesson before the cross-chapter review SA-R06. The punch caution the payoff already claimed is taught only there, so this is where the whole promise can be shown. It now assesses all sixteen atoms the chapter introduces, reaching the gender, sound-law and ञ lessons through added prerequisites.
